newsitem.title: USA: Airlines cancel Colombian flights due to strike.
newsitem.headline: Airlines cancel Colombian flights due to strike.

text.p: Some U.S. airlines said they will cancel flights to and from Colombia Tuesday due to a national public sector strike due to begin at midnight.

About 800,000 state workers in Colombia have called a strike to press for a wage hike of about 21.5 percent, compared to 13.5 percent offered by goverment. Workers are also protesting loss of labor rights and privatization.
Colombia's airport technicians will also join the strike. Air traffic controllers warned there will be delays in all flights and some cancellations.
Continental Airlines Inc and AMR Corp's American Airlines said Monday they would cancel flights on Tuesday, but resume normal operations after the strike, which is expected to last one day.

American said it cancelled one Bogot-bound late flight Monday evening and all flights to and from its three Colombian destinations on Tuesday. Flights originating out of Colombia on Wednesday have also been cancelled.
American serves Bogot, Cali and Baranquilla.
Continental Airlines also said its two daily flights to Colombia have been cancelled for Tuesday.

Even though the airlines are expecting the job action to last a single day, Wilson Borja, head of the main public sector union FENALTRASE, said the strike would continue until the government committed itself in writing to resolving labor demands.
